analysis.investment_thesis: MRPL is a capital-intensive PSU refiner with zero durable competitive advantage — a textbook commodity business where earnings are dictated by crack spreads, not management skill. With ROE of 0.45%, a net profit collapse of 98% YoY (₹3,597 Cr → ₹56 Cr in FY25), and a 9-year net profit CAGR of -21.7%, the business destroys rather than creates shareholder value.
key_strengths: ONGC backing (88.58% promoter) provides financial lifeline and crude supply security during downturns
Debt reduction trajectory: borrowings fell from ₹24,062 Cr (2021) to ₹10,824 Cr (2025), reducing financial fragility
Revenue scale at ₹94,682 Cr with 10.1% 9-year CAGR gives it refinery utilization advantages over smaller peers
key_risks: No economic moat — refining margins (GRMs) are entirely commodity-driven and collapsed in FY25, wiping 98% of net profits
Structurally poor returns: ROE 0.45%, ROCE 4.38% — both well below cost of capital, meaning the business is value-destructive
Extreme earnings volatility: net profit swung from -₹4,043 Cr (2020) to +₹3,597 Cr (2024) to +₹56 Cr (2025) — unpredictability kills intrinsic value estimation
red_flags: FY25 net profit crashed 98% YoY to just ₹56 Cr — P/E of 14.7x is on a near-zero earnings base, masking true overvaluation
EBITDA fell from ₹8,005 Cr (2024) to ₹2,433 Cr (2025) — a 70% collapse in one year reveals zero earnings predictability
FCF cratered from ₹5,509 Cr to ₹918 Cr in one year — dividend sustainability and debt repayment capacity severely impaired
PSU governance: government controls capital allocation decisions, pricing policy, and dividend payouts — minority shareholders are passengers
analysis.detailed_analysis:
MRPL embodies everything I avoid in a business. Oil refining is a brutally competitive commodity industry where the product is indistinguishable and pricing power is nonexistent — the refinery that processes crude cheapest survives, not the one with the best brand. The numbers confirm this: a 9-year EBITDA CAGR of -1.2% and net profit CAGR of -21.7% mean this business has gotten worse in real terms over nearly a decade, despite revenue growing 10% annually on the back of crude price inflation. ROE of 0.45% is not a typo — the company earned essentially nothing on ₹13,318 Cr of equity in FY25.

The FY25 collapse is the story in a single line: net profit fell from ₹3,597 Cr to ₹56 Cr as GRMs compressed, and operating cash flow dropped from ₹7,051 Cr to ₹1,878 Cr. At ₹183/share and 2.41x book, investors are paying a meaningful premium for a PSU that earned 0.45% on equity. The debt reduction since 2021 is the one genuine positive, but with ₹13,143 Cr of total debt still on the books against ₹56 Cr of annual profit, the balance sheet remains hostage to the next margin downturn. I need a business I can predict with confidence for 10 years — MRPL's earnings cannot be predicted for 10 months.
